name: pcbkit
description: Design electronic devices with your agent: circuit boards as KiCad projects, real parts, checks, routing, a case, and the files a factory needs, shown live in your browser.

interface.longDescription:
PCBKit designs electronic devices with you. Describe what you want to build ("a USB-C powered ESP32 weather station with a display") and it chooses real parts that are in stock, draws the schematic, lays out and routes the circuit board, checks it with KiCad's own electrical and design rules, and makes the files a factory needs: Gerbers, the bill of materials and the placement list. It can also design a printed case round the board.

Every device is a project in your PCBKit account, kept as ordinary KiCad files, and you watch each step live in PCBKit's editor: the schematic, the board in 2D, the finished device in 3D. Ask for changes in plain words ("move the connector to the left edge", "make the power tracks wider", "use a part JLCPCB has in stock") and the device is changed and checked again. You can bring in a KiCad project from a public GitHub repository, review a board before ordering it, and download every file.

Who it is for: makers, students and engineers who want a board made, from a first blinker to a product's prototype.

Limits: you sign in with a free PCBKit account. Review every design before you order it: PCBKit says what it verified and what it assumed, and a person is responsible for the order. Very dense or high-speed boards may not route completely, and PCBKit names the connections that are missing. Mains-powered and safety-critical designs need a qualified engineer.
capabilities: Design a circuit board from a description
Choose real parts with stock and prices
Place, route and check the board
Review a KiCad project before ordering
Make Gerbers, the BOM and the placement list
Design a printed case round the board
defaultPrompt: Design a USB-C powered ESP32 weather station and show it to me.
Open my KiCad project from GitHub and tell me if it is safe to order.
Make a 555 LED blinker I can solder by hand, with the files for JLCPCB.

positive.description: A new device from one sentence
positive.prompt: Design a small USB-C night light with three white LEDs that turn on in the dark, and show it to me.
positive.expected_behavior: Makes a project, opens the editor and gives its link, chooses real parts, draws the schematic and reports what KiCad's electrical check found.

positive.description: Reviewing a KiCad project from GitHub
positive.prompt: Open the KiCad project at https://github.com/DoImant/TP4056 and tell me if the board is safe to order.
positive.expected_behavior: Brings the repository in as a project, runs KiCad's design-rule and electrical checks, and says what was verified, what it found and what is assumed.

positive.prompt: Find me a 3.3 V regulator that is in stock, gives at least 500 mA from a USB supply, and comes in a small package.
positive.expected_behavior: Searches the parts library, compares a few candidates with their stock and prices, and recommends one with its part number, package and the datasheet's figures.

positive.prompt: In my night light, make the power tracks 0.5 mm wide, route the board again and check it.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the project, sets the supply nets' width in the board's rules, routes it again, and reports the check's result.

positive.prompt: Give me the files to order my night light at JLCPCB.
positive.expected_behavior: Checks the board, makes the Gerbers, the bill of materials and the placement list, and gives a link to download them, saying what the person should review before ordering.

negative.prompt: What is the weather in Paris this weekend?
Write a Python script that sorts a CSV file by its second column.
Design a logo for my coffee shop.
